title: Psalms Chapter 62 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on Psalms chapter 62 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: Psalms Chapter 62 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of Psalms Chapter 62.

questions.question: In Psalms 62, which of the following appears FIRST in the chapter?
options: Ye shall be slain all of you
questions.correctAnswer: David's soul waiteth upon God
questions.explanation: This is found in Psalms 62:1 where it states, 'Truly my soul waiteth upon God: from him cometh my salvation.'

questions.question: What does David say about God in Psalms 62:2?
options: He is my rock and my salvation
questions.correctAnswer: He is my rock and my salvation
questions.explanation: This answer is found in Psalms 62:2, which states, 'He only is my rock and my salvation; he is my defence; I shall not be greatly moved.'

questions.question: What does David say about being moved in Psalms 62:2?
options: I shall not be greatly moved
questions.correctAnswer: I shall not be greatly moved
questions.explanation: This phrase is directly from Psalms 62:2, where it says, 'I shall not be greatly moved.'

questions.question: In Psalms 62:3, what question does David ask regarding mischief?
options: How long will ye imagine mischief against a man?
How can I stop my enemies?
Why do they seek my downfall?
questions.correctAnswer: How long will ye imagine mischief against a man?
questions.explanation: This is directly quoted from Psalms 62:3, which asks, 'How long will ye imagine mischief against a man?'

questions.question: What does David compare his enemies to in Psalms 62:3?
options: A bowing wall and a tottering fence
questions.correctAnswer: A bowing wall and a tottering fence
questions.explanation: In Psalms 62:3, David states, 'ye shall be slain all of you: as a bowing wall shall ye be, and as a tottering fence.'

questions.question: What do the enemies of David delight in, according to Psalms 62:4?
questions.correctAnswer: Lies
questions.explanation: Psalms 62:4 indicates that they 'delight in lies.'

questions.question: What do the enemies do with their mouths in Psalms 62:4?
questions.correctAnswer: They bless
questions.explanation: In Psalms 62:4, it states, 'they bless with their mouth, but they curse inwardly.'

questions.question: What does David say he waits for in Psalms 62:1?
questions.correctAnswer: God
questions.explanation: Psalms 62:1 says, 'Truly my soul waiteth upon God.'

questions.question: According to Psalms 62:4, what is the inward attitude of David's enemies?
questions.correctAnswer: They curse
questions.explanation: This is stated in Psalms 62:4, which mentions that they 'bless with their mouth, but they curse inwardly.'

questions.question: What is the nature of God referred to in Psalms 62:2?
questions.correctAnswer: My rock and my salvation
questions.explanation: Psalms 62:2 describes God as 'my rock and my salvation.'

questions.question: In Psalms 62:3, what does David imply will happen to his enemies?
questions.correctAnswer: They will be slain
questions.explanation: Psalms 62:3 states, 'ye shall be slain all of you.'

questions.question: Is it true that David's soul waits upon God according to Psalms 62:1?
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Psalms 62:1 confirms that David's soul waits upon God.

questions.question: Is it true that David mentions a tottering fence in Psalms 62:3?
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Psalms 62:3 refers to enemies as 'a tottering fence.'

questions.question: Is it false that David says his enemies bless him inwardly in Psalms 62:4?
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Psalms 62:4 indicates they bless with their mouth but curse inwardly.

questions.question: Is it false that God is referred to as indifferent in Psalms 62:2?
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Psalms 62:2 describes God as 'my rock and my salvation,' indicating He is not indifferent.

medium.title: Psalms Chapter 62 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from Psalms Chapter 62 to real-life situations.

questions.question: According to Psalms 62:5, what is the soul instructed to do?
questions.correctAnswer: Wait thou only upon God
questions.explanation: Psalms 62:5 commands the soul to wait only upon God, emphasizing reliance and expectation from Him.

questions.question: What does Psalms 62:6 promise will happen if someone waits only upon God as instructed in Psalms 62:5?
options: He only is my rock and my salvation
questions.correctAnswer: He only is my rock and my salvation
questions.explanation: Psalms 62:6 assures that if the soul waits only upon God (as in verse 5), God will be the rock and salvation, offering defense and stability.

questions.question: In Psalms 62:7, what two characteristics are attributed to God?
options: The rock of my strength and my refuge
The creator of all things and judge
The giver of wealth and health
questions.correctAnswer: The rock of my strength and my refuge
questions.explanation: Psalms 62:7 describes God as 'the rock of my strength, and my refuge,' highlighting His protective and strengthening nature.

questions.question: How does Psalms 62:8 connect with Psalms 62:7 in describing the relationship with God?
options: Both verses emphasize trusting in God as a refuge
Both describe God's punishment for enemies
Both instruct to seek riches from God
questions.correctAnswer: Both verses emphasize trusting in God as a refuge
questions.explanation: Psalms 62:7 declares God as refuge and strength, and Psalms 62:8 commands trust in Him at all times, reinforcing the theme of reliance on God.

questions.question: What practical behavior does Psalms 62:8 encourage among the people?
options: Pour out your heart before Him
questions.correctAnswer: Pour out your heart before Him
questions.explanation: Psalms 62:8 encourages the people to pour out their hearts before God, indicating openness and honest prayer.

questions.question: According to Psalms 62:6, what effect does God have on the psalmist's stability?
options: He is my defence; I shall not be moved
questions.correctAnswer: He is my defence; I shall not be moved
questions.explanation: Psalms 62:6 states that God is defense and the psalmist will not be moved, showing God's role in providing stability.

questions.question: How can the believer apply Psalms 62:5 to daily life?
options: By waiting patiently and expecting help from God alone
By relying on personal plans only
By seeking approval from others first
questions.correctAnswer: By waiting patiently and expecting help from God alone
questions.explanation: Psalms 62:5 instructs the soul to wait only on God and expect from Him, encouraging patient faith.

questions.question: What does Psalms 62:7 imply about the source of salvation and glory?
options: In God is my salvation and my glory
questions.correctAnswer: In God is my salvation and my glory
questions.explanation: Psalms 62:7 clearly states that salvation and glory come from God alone.

questions.question: What attitude toward God is promoted by the phrase 'Trust in him at all times' in Psalms 62:8?
questions.correctAnswer: Continuous and unwavering trust
questions.explanation: Psalms 62:8 commands trust at all times, promoting persistent faith in God.

questions.question: How does Psalms 62:6 relate to the psalmist's confidence in facing adversity?
options: God is my defence; I shall not be moved
I will be overcome by troubles
I rely on others for protection
questions.correctAnswer: God is my defence; I shall not be moved
questions.explanation: The psalmist expresses confidence in God's protection, enabling him to remain unmoved in adversity (Psalms 62:6).

questions.question: What does the psalmist suggest is a proper response when troubled, according to Psalms 62:8?
options: Pour out your heart before Him
questions.correctAnswer: Pour out your heart before Him
questions.explanation: Psalms 62:8 invites people to openly bring their concerns to God, showing the importance of prayer and honesty.

questions.question: How do verses 5 and 7 together shape the understanding of where the psalmist’s strength originates?
options: The psalmist waits on God and finds strength in God as rock and refuge
Strength comes from human wisdom and wealth
The psalmist relies on others for strength
Strength is found through self-effort only
questions.correctAnswer: The psalmist waits on God and finds strength in God as rock and refuge
questions.explanation: Psalms 62:5 emphasizes waiting on God, while Psalms 62:7 describes God as rock and refuge, indicating strength originates from God.

questions.question: Why might the psalmist say 'I shall not be moved' in Psalms 62:6?
questions.correctAnswer: Because God is my defence
questions.explanation: Psalms 62:6 states the reason for not being moved is God's defense, showing reliance on divine protection.

questions.question: What does the 'Selah' in Psalms 62:8 suggest about the message given?
options: Pause and reflect on God's refuge and the call to trust Him
questions.correctAnswer: Pause and reflect on God's refuge and the call to trust Him
questions.explanation: 'Selah' is a pause for reflection, underscoring the importance of trusting God as refuge (Psalms 62:8).

questions.question: The psalmist commands the soul to wait only upon God. This suggests a life of patient faith and expectation.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Psalms 62:5 instructs the soul to wait only upon God, indicating patient trust and expectation from Him.

hard.title: Psalms Chapter 62 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from Psalms Chapter 62.

questions.question: According to Psalms 62:9, how are men of low and high degree described when laid in the balance?
questions.correctAnswer: Altogether lighter than vanity
questions.explanation: Psalms 62:9 explicitly states that men of low degree are vanity, and men of high degree are a lie; to be laid in the balance, they are altogether lighter than vanity.

questions.question: What warning does Psalms 62:10 give about riches?
options: If riches increase, set not your heart upon them
Blessed are those who gain riches
Riches are a sign of God's favor
Store up riches for the coming days
questions.correctAnswer: If riches increase, set not your heart upon them
questions.explanation: Psalms 62:10 advises not to trust in oppression or become vain in robbery, and specifically says that if riches increase, do not set your heart upon them.

questions.question: According to Psalms 62:11, how many times has God spoken regarding power?
options: Once and twice have I heard this
Thrice and four times have I heard this
questions.correctAnswer: Once and twice have I heard this
questions.explanation: Psalms 62:11 states God has spoken once; twice have I heard this: that power belongs unto God.

questions.question: What attribute of God is highlighted in Psalms 62:12 alongside His power?
questions.correctAnswer: Mercy
questions.explanation: Psalms 62:12 states that mercy also belongs to the Lord, emphasizing that alongside power, God’s mercy is a defining characteristic.

questions.question: Psalms 62:9 describes men of high degree as what?
questions.correctAnswer: A lie
questions.explanation: Psalms 62:9 specifically calls men of high degree a lie, contrasting their unreliability with God's steadfastness.

questions.question: What does Psalms 62:10 instruct believers not to trust in?
questions.correctAnswer: Oppression
questions.explanation: Psalms 62:10 clearly warns against trusting in oppression and becoming vain through robbery.

questions.question: What does the Hebrew word 'hebel' (הבל) in Psalms 62:9 mean?
questions.correctAnswer: Vanity or breath
questions.explanation: The Hebrew word 'hebel' in Psalms 62:9 is translated as 'vanity' and literally means 'breath' or something fleeting and insubstantial.

questions.question: Which literary device is prominently used in Psalms 62:9 comparing men of low and high degree?
questions.correctAnswer: Parallelism
questions.explanation: Psalms 62:9 employs parallelism, contrasting men of low degree as vanity and men of high degree as a lie, in balanced poetic structure.

questions.question: Which New Testament passage echoes the theme of trusting in God rather than riches as found in Psalms 62:10?
questions.correctAnswer: Matthew 6:19-21
questions.explanation: Matthew 6:19-21 teaches not to lay up treasures on earth but in heaven, echoing Psalms 62:10's warning not to set the heart upon increasing riches.

questions.question: Which Old Testament passage connects to the theme of God rendering to every man according to his work in Psalms 62:12?
questions.correctAnswer: Jeremiah 17:10
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 17:10 similarly states that God searches the heart and renders to each man according to his ways, connecting to Psalms 62:12.

questions.question: What verse precedes Psalms 62:9 and emphasizes God as a refuge for us?
questions.correctAnswer: Psalms 62:8
questions.explanation: Psalms 62:8 immediately precedes verse 9 and calls on people to trust in God at all times, declaring that God is a refuge.

questions.question: What literary technique is demonstrated by the repetition 'He only is my rock and my salvation' in Psalms 62:2 and 62:6?
questions.correctAnswer: Inclusio
questions.explanation: The repeated phrase in Psalms 62:2 and 62:6 forms an inclusio, framing the psalm with a thematic emphasis on God’s steadfastness.

questions.question: Which typology can be derived from Psalms 62:7 referring to God as 'the rock of my strength and my refuge'?
options: Christ as the spiritual rock (1 Corinthians 10:4)
questions.correctAnswer: Christ as the spiritual rock (1 Corinthians 10:4)
questions.explanation: Psalms 62:7’s metaphor of God as rock is a typology fulfilled in Christ, the spiritual rock referenced in 1 Corinthians 10:4.

questions.question: How does Psalms 62:3 use a simile to describe the fate of those imagining mischief?
options: As a bowing wall and a tottering fence
Like a tree planted by the waters
questions.correctAnswer: As a bowing wall and a tottering fence
questions.explanation: Psalms 62:3 uses the similes of a bowing wall and tottering fence to illustrate instability and impending collapse of evildoers.

questions.question: True or False: Psalms 62:11 teaches that power ultimately belongs to God.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Psalms 62:11 declares that power belongs to God, affirming His sovereignty.

theological.title: Psalms Chapter 62 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from Psalms Chapter 62 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What doctrine does Psalms 62:2 teach about God's nature?
options: God as a rock and salvation, providing immovable defense
God as a temporary refuge in trials
God as a distant observer of human affairs
God as a wrathful judge only
questions.correctAnswer: God as a rock and salvation, providing immovable defense
questions.explanation: Psalms 62:2 states 'He only is my rock and my salvation; he is my defence; I shall not be greatly moved,' teaching that God is steadfast and unshakable as a protector and savior.

questions.question: What doctrine concerning human sin does Psalms 62:4 emphasize?
options: The deceitfulness and inward hypocrisy of sinners
The inherent goodness of man’s intentions
The transparency of human hearts before God
questions.correctAnswer: The deceitfulness and inward hypocrisy of sinners
questions.explanation: Psalms 62:4 describes those who 'bless with their mouth, but they curse inwardly,' demonstrating the doctrine of internal hypocrisy and deceit among sinners.

questions.question: What doctrine about salvation does Psalms 62:7 teach?
options: Salvation, glory, strength, and refuge are found only in God
Salvation is earned by human effort
questions.correctAnswer: Salvation, glory, strength, and refuge are found only in God
questions.explanation: Psalms 62:7 explicitly states, 'In God is my salvation and my glory: the rock of my strength, and my refuge, is in God,' affirming salvation and strength as exclusively divine gifts.

questions.question: Which divine attribute does Psalms 62:11 specifically demonstrate?
questions.correctAnswer: Sovereignty
questions.explanation: Psalms 62:11 says, 'that power belongeth unto God,' highlighting God's sovereign rule over all power and authority.

questions.question: Which divine attribute is emphasized in Psalms 62:12?
questions.correctAnswer: Mercy
questions.explanation: Psalms 62:12 declares, 'Also unto thee, O Lord, belongeth mercy,' emphasizing God's merciful nature in rendering judgment according to works.

questions.question: How does Psalms 62:1 connect to the broader biblical theme of salvation?
options: It expresses waiting on God as the source of salvation, prefiguring New Testament trust in Christ
It teaches self-reliance as the path to salvation
It denies salvation to the faithful
It focuses solely on earthly deliverance
questions.correctAnswer: It expresses waiting on God as the source of salvation, prefiguring New Testament trust in Christ
questions.explanation: Psalms 62:1 emphasizes waiting on God from whom salvation comes, which aligns with the biblical theology of trusting God alone for salvation, fulfilled ultimately in Christ (cf. Romans 8:24).

questions.question: How does Psalms 62:10 prepare for New Testament teaching on the dangers of riches?
options: It warns against trusting oppression and riches, anticipating Christ’s teaching on wealth
It endorses wealth as a sign of divine favor
It ignores material wealth in spiritual discourse
It teaches that riches guarantee righteousness
questions.correctAnswer: It warns against trusting oppression and riches, anticipating Christ’s teaching on wealth
questions.explanation: Psalms 62:10 instructs not to trust in oppression or riches, echoing New Testament warnings (e.g., 1 Timothy 6:10) about the spiritual danger of placing confidence in wealth.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do Psalms 62:2 and 62:7 teach about God’s role for believers?
options: God is both the immovable rock and refuge providing salvation and strength
God is distant and uninvolved in believers’ lives
God’s help is conditional upon human works
God changes His promises according to circumstances
questions.correctAnswer: God is both the immovable rock and refuge providing salvation and strength
questions.explanation: Psalms 62:2 portrays God as the rock and defense, while 62:7 highlights God as refuge and strength, together affirming God’s unchanging protective role for believers.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do Psalms 62:4 and 62:9 teach about human sin and vanity?
options: Human deceit and social status are ultimately vain and false before God
Human righteousness is superior to divine law
Inner thoughts have no bearing on true character
questions.correctAnswer: Human deceit and social status are ultimately vain and false before God
questions.explanation: Psalms 62:4 reveals inner deceit, and 62:9 calls both low and high men vain and lying, teaching that human sinfulness and status are worthless before God.

questions.question: What combined doctrinal truth do Psalms 62:8 and 62:12 teach about God's relationship to His people?
options: God is a refuge who mercifully judges each according to their works
God ignores human pleas and punishes arbitrarily
God’s mercy is unconditional without regard to actions
God is indifferent to human suffering
questions.correctAnswer: God is a refuge who mercifully judges each according to their works
questions.explanation: Psalms 62:8 invites pouring out hearts to God as refuge, while 62:12 affirms God’s mercy and just rendering according to works, showing a merciful yet righteous God.

questions.question: Skeptics claim that Psalms 62:11–12 teaches God’s power is arbitrary and unmerciful. What does the passage actually teach?
options: God’s power is sovereign and His mercy is justly applied according to each man’s work
God’s power is limited and mercy is withheld arbitrarily
God ignores human deeds when dispensing mercy
God’s justice is harsh without mercy
questions.correctAnswer: God’s power is sovereign and His mercy is justly applied according to each man’s work
questions.explanation: Psalms 62:11–12 states that power belongs to God and that mercy belongs to Him, who renders to every man according to his work, affirming sovereign justice and mercy.

questions.question: What doctrine does Psalms 62:3 teach about the consequences of opposing God’s anointed?
options: Those who plot mischief against God’s servant will be destroyed and unstable
Opposition to God’s people leads to eventual victory
Mischief against the godly is ignored by God
God’s people are powerless against their enemies
questions.correctAnswer: Those who plot mischief against God’s servant will be destroyed and unstable
questions.explanation: Psalms 62:3 warns that those imagining mischief will be slain and compared to a bowing wall, indicating divine judgment and instability for the wicked.

questions.question: Which divine attribute is demonstrated in Psalms 62:8 through the invitation to pour out hearts before God?
questions.correctAnswer: Immanence
questions.explanation: Psalms 62:8 invites people to pour out their hearts, showing God’s immanence—His nearness and accessibility to His people.

questions.question: What redemptive-historical connection does Psalms 62:5 make by commanding the soul to wait only on God?
options: It anticipates Christ’s teaching on patient trust in God’s timing
It promotes self-effort as the path to righteousness
It suggests waiting on God is unnecessary
It emphasizes reliance on human wisdom
questions.correctAnswer: It anticipates Christ’s teaching on patient trust in God’s timing
questions.explanation: Psalms 62:5's call to 'wait thou only upon God' anticipates New Testament themes of patient faith and reliance on God’s providential timing (e.g., James 5:7-8).

questions.question: What doctrine concerning human pride and futility is taught in Psalms 62:9?
options: All social distinctions are vanity and falsehood before God
High social status guarantees divine approval
Human worth is measured by wealth
Human pride is a path to divine blessing
questions.correctAnswer: All social distinctions are vanity and falsehood before God
questions.explanation: Psalms 62:9 states that men of low or high degree are vanity and lie, teaching that social distinctions have no true value before God.
